Consider the same gate for active mode, or state in the docs that the check is manual. fix round 1 rule: evaluate() derives read scope the way spawn does (reuse spawn's read-scope derivation or accept read_scope as an explicit keyword computed by the daemon from the same helper) and never reads a task field that bus tasks do not carry; add a test with a real-shaped bus task (no read_scope key) where triggers still fire. Shadow rows: write a row only when the action is not continue or the (trigger, evidence_hash) differs from the task's last row, so plain continue ticks do not flood decisions.jsonl; recent() reads only steering rows for the task, not a global 500-row window. steering_tick must not call harness_depth.begin_tick or re-run promotion.evaluate for fast_path: reuse the tick's existing harness_depth result passed in, and return early before any state change when steering mode is off. git status runs with --untracked-files=all so new in-scope directories are not counted as out of scope. Active mode is gated on promotion.evaluate('steering_policy') like fast_path (refuse to shadow with a notify when criteria are unmet), and the docs say so. Run .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh . until it exits 0; do not ask questions; report files changed and failures-only output.

result.summary: All five review findings are addressed and the acceptance tests exist. Two medium issues remain: one is notification spam, the other is a full-file log scan on every tick. I read the diff only and did not run the suite.

comments.issue: When active mode is refused by the promotion gate, notify() fires on every tick for as long as the criteria stay unmet. test_active_promotion_refusal_uses_shadow asserts one notification per tick. That floods the notification channel. Also, promotion.collect re-reads the decision log on every tick in active mode. Notify only when the refusal reasons change, or once per interval.

recent(kind, subject) scans backwards until it finds `limit` matching rows. A task normally has far fewer than 500 steering rows, so each call reads and json-parses the whole decisions.jsonl. _steering_decisions calls it once per running task per tick, which makes tick cost grow with total log size times the number of running tasks. Use a much smaller limit (only the last row and the applied rows are needed), or read the log once per tick and group by subject.

Fix-round and token criteria for steering_policy are now skipped whenever active_n is 0. Active mode can therefore be promoted on shadow_n >= 20 alone. This is needed to bootstrap, but it means the fix-round criteria are only enforced after the first active row. The docs should say so. Separately, shadow_n now counts distinct root task ids instead of shadow rows, which is a stricter, unrequested change. Confirm that was intended.

read_scope() duplicates the spawn._packet_body derivation instead of reusing it, so the two can drift apart. It also joins task scope entries onto the worktree without a containment check. Extract a shared helper used by both, and skip scope entries that resolve outside the worktree.
